summary: Alfred Gell studied at the London School of Economics and Political Science from around 1968 to 1971. He later held a post there from approximately 1979 to 1997.

Alfred Hillebrandt was an Indologist who studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler (~1871-1875) and at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1875-1876). He served as a professor at the University of Breslau from around 1883 to 1922.

Indologist and linguist Alfred Ludwig studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin under Moriz Haupt, Friedrich Müller, Anton Boller, and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at the University of Vienna and Charles University.

Alicia Turner is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Chicago. Her doctoral supervisors were Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins, and her teachers included Saw Tun, Daw Than Than Win, and Carol S. Anderson.

Alison Denton Jones works in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She was supervised by doctoral supervisor Martin King Whyte and also studied under Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret Dornish.

Allan G. Grapard was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. Between approximately 1985 and 2007, he served as ISF Professor of Shinto Studies at the University of California and taught in the Department of Religious Studies at UC Santa Barbara.

Philosopher Allan Gibbard studied at Swarthmore College (~1960-1964) and Harvard University (~1965-1971). He held positions at the University of Chicago (~1969-1974), the University of Pittsburgh (~1974-1977), and the University of Michigan (around 1977).
Sinologist Allan H. Barr completed his doctorate at the University of Oxford by 1983. As of 2001, he held a post as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College.

Indologist Allen Wright Thrasher completed doctoral studies under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and received traditional instruction from Vighnahari Bhalacandra Deo, R. Srinivasan Raghavachariar, and K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri. He held a post at the Library of Congress around 1984.

Alnis Dickson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed an MA at McGill University, attested in 2009. His MA supervisor was Lara Braitstein, and he also studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Aloys Sprenger, an Indologist, studied at the University of Vienna (~1832-1836). He served as principal of Delhi College (~1845-1848), Hooghly Mohsin College (1851-1854), and Aliah University (~1850-1856), before holding a post at the University of Bern (~1858-1881).

Alvappillai Veluppillai studied at the University of Oxford (~1967-1971). A scholar of Indology, religious studies, and linguistics, he held posts at the Universities of Kerala, Edinburgh, Virginia, Uppsala (~1990-2000), and Arizona State University (~1990-2000).

Amalananda Ghosh was an archaeologist, historian, and Indologist who studied at University College London. He served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India from around 1953 to 1968.

Amanda K. Goodman, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, supervised by Robert H. Sharf, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr. She holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.

Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed doctoral studies under Anthony Kennedy Warder. He also studied under Rahul Sankrityayan, Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, and Alasdair Urquhart.

Amaranatha Jha studied at Muir Central College, where he became Professor of English in 1917. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938-1946) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947-1948), and was Vice-President of the Ganganatha Jha Research Institute.

Amber D. Carpenter is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under teachers including M. M. McCabe. She held posts at St Andrews, the Einstein Forum, the University of York, and as an associate professor at Yale-NUS College.

Amelia Hall is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her doctorate from the University of Oxford by 2012. Her attested appointments in 2019 include Naropa University and Central Michigan University.
Amita Chatterjee is an Indologist and philosopher who held positions as professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, attested in 1999 and 2009.
Amod Lele is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Parimal G. Patil.
